text: Can you describe the exact nature of your right groin pain and how your leg is positioned right now? I need to know if you can actively move your hip or if it feels locked in a specific posture.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify if your right leg appears shortened and externally rotated, which are classic signs of a hip fracture or dislocation. Can you also tell me if you were wearing a seatbelt at the time of the collision? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms a posterior dislocation of the right hip, which is consistent with the dashboard injury mechanism. We need to proceed with urgent closed reduction to prevent avascular necrosis of the femoral head. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The physical exam findings of a shortened, internally rotated leg confirm the posterior hip dislocation despite the X-ray ambiguity. I will now proceed with an urgent closed reduction under sedation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation
